title: Formal Logic
alt: Note that this implies you should NOT honk solely because I stopped for a pedestrian and you're behind me.
transcript:
[The rear end of a car (with an unreadable license plate), with a bumper sticker above the tailpipe to the right:]
Honk iff you love
formal logic
explanation:
This comic is a riff on bumper stickers that say "honk if you love ____". Here, the subject is , but the word "if" is replaced with a formal logic term "," which means "if and only if". 

The term "If and only if" stipulates that the truth value of both cause and effect (or similarly tied conditions) must be the same. When evaluating one statement based on another, if the condition statement is true, then the conclusion statement must be true, and if the condition statement is false the conclusion must be false. (This is distinct from a simple "if", which leaves the conclusion undefined or unaltered where the condition is false.) In this case, you must honk if you love formal logic, and you are only allowed to honk if you love formal logic (in other words, someone who does not love formal logic is prohibited from honking). The title text elaborates on this, saying, in essence, "Don't honk at me just because you're impatient that I stopped for a pedestrian."

The sticker is somewhat self-referential: you have to love formal logic to take the sticker seriously and honk for exclusively that reason. The title text reveals the sticker is actually there to stop people from honking at Randall altogether, because, understandably, he hates it when he yields for pedestrians only to get honked at by some impatient driver behind him. The ONLY reason the sticker allows you to honk is to declare your love for formal logic. By extension, if someone DOES honk while he is stopped for a pedestrian, he can simply enjoy the idea that the other driver loves formal logic rather than being impatient, transforming what might otherwise be an irritant into pleasure.
